title: introduce-kernel-eviction-prober-with-prefetch-coalescer-simulator
author: Evan Cho
description:
Motivation: reproduce realistic memory-pressure scenarios that cause transient kernel eviction and prefetch coalescing behavior observed on GPU backends, then surface their latency/throughput impact in our benchmark lab. This PR adds a lightweight simulator that injects eviction events at configurable phases, a prefetch coalescer model that emulates how upstream request priming changes kernel occupancy, and a compact reporter that correlates eviction events with p95/p99 token tail amplification.

What I changed: added an eviction prober harness (go) that can run as part of existing workload runners, introduced a prefetch-coalescer phase model (python) used by the microworkload generator, and a reporter plugin to export eviction-aligned latencies and a per-kernel occupancy timeline to the telemetry pipeline. The goal is not to replace hardware-level profilers but to provide a deterministic, repeatable synthetic that surfaces the class of regressions we keep hitting in nightly canaries.

Key features and knobs: --evict-rate (0..1) to probabilistically emit eviction signals, --evict-phase to align evictions with primer/response windows, prefetch_profile YAML to define primer sizes and coalescing thresholds, optional --attach-kernel-hint to annotate which kernel family should be blamed. The reporter emits metrics: bench.eviction.count, bench.eviction.aligned_p95, bench.eviction.aligned_p99, bench.kernel.occupancy.timeline (compact tokenized string), and a CSV export for offline correlation.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for the coalescer math and deterministic RNG seeding, an integration bench that runs the prober across three occupancy profiles (sparse, mixed, dense) and asserts no more than 5% nondeterministic variance in p95 across seeds. The PR includes a new nightly canary job (bench-eviction-prober) that runs the integration bench on a small cluster of GPUs to catch regressions during kernel changes.

Why this is important: several recent regressions (see linked Linear tickets) were only visible when eviction-like interference occurred alongside primer-heavy workloads. This harness lets us reproduce those scenarios in CI and add stable baselines to the perf dashboard so we can detect regressions earlier.

Checklist: [x] Simulator scaffolded and documented, [x] Reporter + metrics wired into telemetry, [x] Unit + integration tests, [x] CI job added, [ ] Add end-to-end dashboard panels (follow-up ENG-1438).

release_notes: Add a benchmark harness that simulates kernel eviction events and prefetch coalescing to surface memory-pressure regressions. Includes reporter metrics and a nightly canary job.
review_comments: Maya Kline (reviewer): Can we make the eviction RNG seed deterministic in CI runs so nightly baselines are reproducible? Also request clearer names for the occupancy timeline encoding.
Evan Cho (author): Added deterministic seeding and documented the timeline encoding (compact base64 token stream) in docs/bench/eviction-prober.md.

Rajat Sharma (reviewer): The coalescer model looks good but please add a short validation test that compares the model output to a small empirical trace we have in fixtures/ (helps prevent drift when we tweak math).
Evan Cho (author): Added validation test using fixtures/empirical_coalesce_trace.json and a tolerance assertion.
summary_of_changes: Introduce eviction simulator, prefetch coalescer, eviction-aligned reporter, tests, and CI job to detect memory-pressure related regressions.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the coalescer math and the telemetry labels. The occupancy timeline is intentionally compact to limit cardinality; if you need expanded traces the CSV output can be used for offline analysis.
